More than half of the final stories must originate with independent, local or social discovery, using the first source in each story as the discovery source; established outlets may account for no more than half.

items.title: Will affect election: Calcutta HC dismisses plea flagging age discrepancy in BJP candidate Hasirani Rath's affidavit
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court recently dismissed a plea by the West Bengal Congress seeking verification of an alleged discrepancy in the election affidavit of Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) Nandigram bye-election candidate Hasirani Rath [West Bengal Pradesh Congress Committee & Anr. v Election Committee of India & Ors] . Justice Krishna Rao held that deciding the issue at this stage would interfere with the ongoing election process. "If at this stage, this Court will decide the issue raised by the petitioner No. 2 (Mita Chakraborty, Congress leader) with regard to the nomination papers of the respondent no. 5 (Hasirani Rath), the same will directly affects the present election process," said the Court. The by-election is scheduled to be held on October 6. Justice Krishna Rao Rath was announced as the BJP's candidate on September 15. The seat fell vacant after BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari, who had won both Nandigram and Bhabanipur in the 2026 Assembly election, retained the latter seat. items.title: Calcutta High Court grants interim bail to Congress candidate Milan Pradhan to contest Nandigram by-polls
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on Tuesday granted interim bail to Congress leader Milan Pradhan to enable him to contest the upcoming Nandigram bypolls. Pradhan has been in custody in connection with six cases relating to the 2007 Nandigram violence. Justice Tirthankar Ghosh today ordered that Pradhan be released on interim bail till October 20 provided he furnishes a bond of ₹20,000 along with two sureties of ₹10,000 each. " I am of the opinion that petitioner may be granted an opportunity to contest the election and to that effect he may be released on interim bail," the Court said. The direction was part of separate orders passed on six bail pleas filed by Pradhan in connection with his arrest in six criminal cases from 2007, which involved allegations of rioting and murder. Justice Tirthankar Ghosh In his petitions, Pradhan questioned the timing of his arrest, given that the cases against him were from nearly two decades ago. His counsel pointed out that the police waited till after Pradhan filed his nomination papers for the Nandigram bypolls to execute arrest warrants for the first time in 19 years. items.title: One school, zero scrutiny: How ANI, News18 sold Gujarat’s school ‘model’
items.summary: As the Cockroach Janta Party’s ‘School Thik Karo’ campaign draws national attention to the state of government schools, ANI and News18 Gujarati have gone the other way – holding up a single school in Gujarat’s Botad district as evidence that the state’s public education system is flourishing. Both outlets built their stories around PM SHRI Dr Sarvapalli Radhakrishnan Nagar Primary School No. 24, citing long waiting lists and parents choosing it over private options. News18 ’s headline claimed the school “puts private schools to shame”. ANI ’s three-minute video carried interviews with the principal, students and parents, framing it much the same way: 250 children on a waiting list, government schools becoming parents’ “top choice”. Neither outlet disclosed whether the coverage was paid promotion, and neither offered the wider picture. Moreover, government data tells a starkly different story. According to the Ministry of Education’s UDISE+ report , only 54.5 percent of Gujarat’s 1.15 crore government-school students complete their education through Class 12. items.title: Is the master of roster mastering the roster?
items.summary: The Chief Justice is the master of the roster. But when control of the roster determines which judge hears which sensitive case, the question is no longer merely administrative. It is about who decides which cases are heard and by whom - and whether the established norms of roster allocation are being followed. The Medha Roopam listing: Where did the roster go? The controversy begins with a case that should have been routine: a challenge by Gautam Buddha Nagar District Magistrate Medha Roopam to the Allahabad High Court judgment quashing the National Security Act detention of Delhi University student Akriti Chaudhary. The Supreme Court matter was heard on September 23 by Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N Kotiswar Singh . The difficulty is that the published roster did not ordinarily assign habeas corpus and preventive detention matters to Justice Sharma’s Bench. That category was assigned to a Bench headed by Justice BV Nagarathna . A special assignment is not, by itself, unlawful. But that is precisely why the question cannot be brushed aside: who authorised the departure from the ordinary roster and where is that departure recorded? items.summary: A curative petition has been filed before the Supreme Court seeking recall of its recent split verdict on the need to refer the petitions challenging the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 to a larger bench. The petition filed by Dr Jaya Thakur states that Justice Satish Chandra Sharma , who agreed with the Central government's demand to refer the matter to a larger bench, should not have heard the matter on account of a direct conflict of interest. She has argued that there was a "reasonable apprehension of bias and propriety" since Justice Sharma's son, Siddharth Sharma, is a standing counsel for the Election Commission of India (ECI) before the Madhya Pradesh High Court since July 2024. Justice Dipankar Datta had rejected the Centre's request for a reference to a larger bench. A Bench of Justice Datta and Justice Sharma on September 23 had delivered separate views on the petitions challenging Sections 7 and 8 of the 2023 Act, under which the selection panel comprises the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition and a Union Cabinet Minister. items.title: Kerala High Court quashes State decision to abolish Kerala Police Officers Association
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Tuesday quashed the State government's decision to dissolve the Kerala Police Officers Association (KPOA), as part of its move to restructure associations formed by police officers in Kerala [ Kerala Police Officers Association v State of Kerala & connected cases ]. The State Home Department's order was aimed at reorganising three associations representing different ranks of police personnel. The State's move resulted in the dissolution of one of the three police associations (KPOA), while the remaining two were to be retained in a reorganised form. This was challenged before the High Court by the KPOA. Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas today ruled in KPOA's favour, holding that the State did not have the power to restructure the three police associations in the way it did, that its decision interfered with the constitutional right of the police officers to continue in their associations. "The recognition granted to the members of the police force to form associations has not been revoked either by the State Police Chief or even by the government. Hasan had reportedly written that the Allahabad High Court reprimanded the Uttar Pradesh Police over Shamli youth Ayush Malik's illegal confinement at his home . Malik had been illegally detained by his family following his conversion from Hinduism to Islam. The police denied the claim that it was reprimanded by High Court and registered an FIR against Hasan and others. items.title: Thoothukudi firing: A Raja, the cop who fired on protesters, dies of illness
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A Raja, the district armed reserve constable, who was seen firing from atop a police vehicle during the 2018 anti-Sterlite protests in Thoothukudi, died on Tuesday, September 29, after undergoing treatment for health complications. According to reports, Raja had served in the Tamil Nadu police for more than two decades. He joined the police force in 2003 and was serving in the Thoothukudi district armed reserve. He was recently transferred to the law and order wing at the Kulasekarapattinam police station. However, he had not joined his new posting, as he was undergoing treatment for kidney and liver-related ailments. Raja is survived by his wife and two sons, who are pursuing college education. Raja came to public attention after photographs and videos of the police firing during the anti-Sterlite protests in May 2018 were widely circulated. One of the photographs showed a policeman wearing a yellow and black T-shirt, standing atop a police vehicle and firing at the protestors. The policeman was later identified as Raja. items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday clarified that certain directions contained in a May 29 single-judge Bench ruling on the 'right to be forgotten' do not apply to Meta platforms such as Facebook [ Meta Platforms vs Mr X & Ors ]. A Division Bench of Justice C Hari Shankar and Justice Nivedita Anil Sharma issued the clarification, while dealing with a plea moved by Meta in the matter. By a May 29 ruling, a single-judge Bench of the Court had directed search-engine operators, including Google, to de-index certain judicial records from name-based search results. In this regard, the May 29 judgment had said, “The concerned respondents/ search engine operators/ legal data base platforms are directed to de-index, and disable, across all platforms and domains, name-based search functionality in respect of the judgments/orders/news articles complained of in the petition.” It had also directed law database, Indian Kanoon to restrict name-based searches for these records, although the platform was allowed to continue giving users access to these records through other parameters such as case number, citation, court and date. State of Maharashtra] A Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe expressed dissatisfaction with the manner in which the child rights body had responded to the issue. “How can they act so indifferent? items.title: Kerala govt orders vigilance probe into Kochi Life-Mission flat construction defects
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Kerala government has ordered a Vigilance probe into the construction defects, structural compromises, and financial irregularities surrounding the P and T Apartment complex at Mundamveli in Ernakulam. The housing complex, home to 78 families, was built under the LIFE Mission housing scheme and implemented by the Greater Cochin Development Authority (GCDA) to rehabilitate the families who lived in the waterlogging-prone P and Colony. The government order followed an inspection report submitted by the Director of the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB). According to the order, the government has sanctioned a preliminary probe under Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act. Speaking to the media, the apartment’s residents’ association president said the residents welcome the vigilance inquiry. The government order for the vigilance inquiry came days after the Chief Minister VD Satheesan declared that the housing complex would be demolished and residents rehabilitated.
